title: kate-search: plain, whole-word and regex search over a rope; replace as a Transaction
summary: Find and replace as pure functions over TextBuffer. Plain and whole-word search walk rope chunks directly; regex search runs the regex crate over the rope via regex-cursor without copying the text. Replace-all produces one Transaction (so undo is one step) with $1/\1 capture expansion. Kate's three modes map to three Pattern variants and nothing else; the find bar UI is a later packet.

lane.reason: Pure library work against kate-text's public API with property tests; runs in parallel with the kate-syntax lane.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary:
New crate API. Dependencies with justification: regex (linear-time engine; user patterns must not be able to hang the editor, so no fancy-regex here), regex-cursor 0.1 (regex over rope chunks with no full-text copy), ropey 1.6 (simd) (TextBuffer::text returns ropey::Rope, which kate-text does not re-export), log 0.4 (transitive via regex-cursor). Pattern escapes are 
, 	, \xNN, \uNNNN and \. Any other escape, a short hex run, a trailing \ or a surrogate returns InvalidEscape { at = byte index of the \ }. replace_all with Pattern::Plain inserts the replacement literally. EscapeSequences and Regex expand $0-$9, ${N}, \0-\9, $$, \, 
 and 	, and an unknown \X drops the backslash. A missing \N writes the digit N. A missing $N or ${N} writes empty text. ${name} resolves only for Regex. whole_words reports every hit whose neighbouring scalars are both non-\w (Unicode \w). A rejected candidate does not hide an overlapping later hit, because the scan restarts one scalar later. Pattern::Regex ignores the flag. Regex uses multi_line, `.` excludes 
, and \s is not rewritten to [ 	]. An empty Plain pattern yields an empty hit at each scalar boundary (str::match_indices). Case-insensitive plain search uses to_lowercase, not full case folding, so ß does not match ss. replace_all drops an edit that would overlap the previous one. It is one transaction (one undo step), and it is linear in the number of matches.

regression_tests.name: search::tests::plain_search_agrees_with_str_match_indices
regression_tests.asserts: For random text and needle, find_all ranges equal std's match_indices converted to char offsets, for both case modes.

regression_tests.name: search::tests::regex_over_chunk_boundary_matches
regression_tests.asserts: A match that straddles a rope chunk boundary in a 1 MiB buffer is found with the correct range.

regression_tests.name: search::tests::replace_all_is_one_transaction_and_undoes_in_one_step
regression_tests.asserts: replace_all on 1000 matches yields a Transaction with 1000 edits; applying it and then its inverse restores the buffer; count == 1000.

regression_tests.name: search::tests::find_next_wraps_and_terminates
regression_tests.asserts: find_next with wrap from the last match returns the first; from a buffer with no match returns None; an empty-match regex does not loop.
